$janet.$comment: Not JSON Schema. Read by scripts/Test-OutputContracts.ps1, which is the point of the file living here rather than being generated from the return type.
$janet.$comment.contractField: The envelope stamps 'contract' and the gate cross-checks it against the number above, so code and schema cannot drift apart in either direction.
$janet.$comment.noRequestHeaders: There is deliberately no field that echoes the request headers. They may carry a caller's credentials, and the envelope lands in a transcript that is written to disk and re-sent every turn; adding such a field is a change of purpose, not of format.
$janet.$comment.everyKey: Every key is always present; a value that does not apply is null rather than absent.

contract.description: Bumped only by a format change. An engine change that moves this number is a mistake in one direction; a format change that does not is a mistake in the other.

url.description: The URL as the caller passed it.

method.description: The method, upper-cased. Only GET, HEAD and OPTIONS are ever sent; anything else is refused, which is what keeps the tool read-only.

expectStatus.description: The status the caller called success, or null for any 2xx.

warmingStatuses.description: The statuses that were retried on, echoed so a reader can tell a deliberate stop from an exhausted wait. No HTTP answer at all is always retried and is not listed here.

ok.description: True when the final status equals expectStatus (or is any 2xx when that is null) and the body was read without error. False for a refused request, a transport failure, a warm-up that never ended, and a definitive other status alike; 'attempts' and 'error' say which.

status.description: The final attempt's HTTP status, or null when it got no HTTP answer at all.

reason.description: The final response's reason phrase as the server sent it, or null with no response. HTTP/2 has none, so it may be null beside a status.

elapsedMs.description: Milliseconds for the whole probe, every attempt and every delay between them. Each attempt's own time is in 'attempts'.

attempts.description: One entry per request sent, in order. Empty only when the request was refused before anything was sent.

status.description: This attempt's HTTP status, or null for no HTTP answer.

elapsedMs.description: From sending this request to its last body byte read, or to its failure.

outcome.description: matched: the status the caller wanted, so the probe stopped. warming: a status in warmingStatuses, so it asked again if retries remained. noResponse: no HTTP answer (refused, reset, DNS, TLS, timeout), which is warming too. unexpected: any other status, which ends the probe because asking again would only repeat it.

error.description: Why this attempt had no answer, or no whole body; null when it had both.

headers.description: The final response's headers in the order received, a repeated one's values joined with ', '. Only the named ones when the caller named some; otherwise all, up to 50.

name.description: The header name as the server sent it.

headersTruncated.description: True when the response had more headers than the 50 returned. Never true when the caller named the headers it wanted.

body.description: The final response's body, at most bodyCap bytes, decoded as UTF-8 with anything undecodable as U+FFFD. Empty for an empty body or a HEAD; null when there was no response.

bodyBytes.description: How many bytes of body were read into 'body'. Not the response's full length, which the probe deliberately does not read past the cap to learn.

bodyTruncated.description: True when the body went on past bodyCap. The probe reads one byte beyond the cap to know, and no further.

error.description: The final attempt's transport failure, or 'refused: ...' when the request was never sent (not http or https, a method that could change something, a value out of range, a header that cannot be sent). A header is named by position and name, never by value. Null when the final attempt was answered in full.
